main_text.p: Possedit, ducente Deo, lato vbere terram. Arborei fœtus hîc curvant pondere ramos, Pafcua lata virent, nec non melioribus herbis, Grano triticeo grandidas effundit aristas Pinguis ager, fœto turgent in palmite gemmæ, Atque inculta rubent multis dumeta racemis: Mellefluunt duri silices, & nectare quercus, Liquuntur & cautes lacrymis oleique, merique, Et pretiosa ipsa sudant opobalsama sylua.

Hîc Deus ingratos Isaci aluisse nepotes Sustinuit, vitaque dedit pecuaria gentis, Balantumque greges, tauros, hirtaque capellas, Dimitis exuvias populi, & congesta metalla Viscera telluris totfossa laboribus, & quæ Gens male sana suum parce feruabat in usum.
Felix, ô nimium felix, si grata fuisset Progenies Hebraea Patris sed non memor alti Fœdauit tot dona Dei, tot munera, tamque Illustres palmas, partofque ex hoste triumphos.

Ebria deliciis terra saturataque ritus Polluit antiquos, latasque in vertice montis Iuratasque atauis leges, cum territa vultu Diuino attoniti tremuere cacumina Sinæ, Diffiluitque solum, vastufque immugiit æther.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "granidas" (may be grandidas), "Mellefluunt", "Dimitis" (may be Dinitis), "Isaci", "partofque" and "vastufque" are as printed in the scan's long-s forms, and the stanza breaks are inferred from the indents. "Mell" and "Liquuntur" may contain printing errors. The line "IDEM" is set alone at the foot right and is kept as a paragraph, not a catchword.
